subChunks.title: State Variants
subChunks.hookHtml: A form input that looks identical whether focused or blurred is a usability failure. A button with no hover state feels like a static image. State variants let you apply utilities only when an element is in a specific condition — hover, focus, disabled, checked, even when a parent or sibling is in a certain state.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Core interactive states

hover:bg-blue-700         /* pointer is over the element */
focus:ring-2              /* element has focus (any method) */
focus-visible:ring-2      /* element focused via KEYBOARD only */
active:scale-95           /* element is being pressed */
disabled:opacity-50       /* element has disabled attribute */
checked:bg-blue-600       /* checkbox/radio is checked */

focus vs focus-visible — the accessible distinction

focus: fires when the element receives focus by any means — mouse click, keyboard Tab, or programmatic. focus-visible: only fires when the browser determines the user is navigating by keyboard. This is the correct choice for focus rings on buttons — it keeps the UI clean for mouse users while fully supporting keyboard navigation.

/* Buttons: use focus-visible so ring only shows for keyboard users */
focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 focus-visible:ring-offset-2

/* Inputs: use focus because ALL focus on an input should be visible */
focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:border-blue-500

Placeholder and validation states

placeholder:text-gray-400       /* style the placeholder text */
placeholder:italic

invalid:border-red-500          /* fails HTML5 validation */
valid:border-green-500          /* passes HTML5 validation */

Parent state — group

<div class="group cursor-pointer p-6 border rounded-xl hover:border-blue-300 transition-colors">
  <h3 class="group-hover:text-blue-600 transition-colors">Title</h3>
  <span class="opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition-opacity">→</span>
</div>

Add group to the parent. Any descendant can use group-hover:, group-focus: to react to the parent's state.

Sibling state — peer

<!-- Custom toggle: checkbox drives label style -->
<input type="checkbox" id="accept" class="peer sr-only" />
<label for="accept" class="
  border-2 border-gray-200 rounded-lg p-3 cursor-pointer
  peer-checked:border-blue-500 peer-checked:bg-blue-50
">
  Accept Terms
</label>

Add peer to an element. A following sibling can then react to its state with peer-checked:, peer-focus:, etc.

Structural variants

first:rounded-t-lg    /* first child only */
last:rounded-b-lg     /* last child only */
odd:bg-gray-50        /* every odd-numbered child */
even:bg-white         /* every even-numbered child */

ARIA state variants

aria-checked:bg-blue-600    /* element has aria-checked="true" */
aria-expanded:rotate-180    /* element has aria-expanded="true" */
aria-disabled:opacity-50    /* element has aria-disabled="true" */

In React — let CSS handle disabled states

/* Old way: conditional className logic */
<button className={isLoading ? 'opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed' : ''} />

/* Tailwind way: disabled: variant reads the DOM attribute */
<button
  className="disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed"
  disabled={isLoading}
/>

Master Ember: "focus-visible: rather than focus: on rings. Mouse users clicking a button don't need a ring — they can see where they clicked. Keyboard users tabbing to it do. focus-visible gives you both without compromise."

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: Static elements are dead elements. Every interactive piece needs to respond to the user. Hover, focus, active, disabled — these are not cosmetic concerns. A form input with no visible focus state is inaccessible to keyboard users.

storyBeats.speaker: Accessible button with all states
storyBeats.text:
<button class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 active:scale-95
               focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 focus-visible:ring-offset-2
               disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed
               text-white px-4 py-2 rounded-md transition-all">
  Submit
</button>

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a form input with proper interactive states:

  • .input-wrapper: relative, flex, flex-col, gap-1
  • .input-label: text-sm, font-medium, text-gray-700
  • .input-field: w-full, px-3, py-2, border, border-gray-300, rounded-md, text-sm, placeholder:text-gray-400, focus:outline-none, focus:ring-2, focus:ring-blue-500, focus:border-blue-500, disabled:bg-gray-50, disabled:cursor-not-allowed
  • .submit-btn: w-full, py-2, px-4, bg-blue-600, hover:bg-blue-700, active:bg-blue-800, disabled:opacity-50, disabled:cursor-not-allowed, text-white, font-medium, rounded-md, transition-colors
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a settings card with: a toggle switch using peer (checkbox peer, label uses peer-checked: to change background and border colour), a hover-lift card effect, and a text input with visible focus ring. No scaffolding provided.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the difference between focus: and focus-visible: variants. When would you use each, and why does the distinction matter for accessibility? Walk through the peer pattern for a custom checkbox — what does peer do, and why must the peer-checked: element come after the peer element in the HTML?

questions.prompt: Which variant applies a utility only when the element receives keyboard focus (not mouse click)?
questions.explanation: focus-visible: maps to the CSS :focus-visible pseudo-class, which the browser only activates when it determines the user is navigating by keyboard. This is the correct choice for focus rings on interactive elements.

questions.prompt: You have a card that should darken its title and reveal a hidden arrow when the entire card is hovered. What is the correct Tailwind approach?
options: Add group to the card, use group-hover: on the title and arrow
Add hover: to both the title and arrow individually
Use JavaScript to add/remove classes on mouseover
Use peer on the card and peer-hover: on children
questions.answer: Add group to the card, use group-hover: on the title and arrow
questions.explanation: group on the parent and group-hover: on children is the Tailwind pattern for parent-triggered child states. peer is for sibling relationships (a following sibling reacts to the peer element's state), not parent-child relationships.

questions.prompt: A developer styles a custom toggle using checked:bg-blue-600 on a <div> element. The toggle state is tracked in React but the checked: variant never applies. Why doesn't it work?
options: checked: targets the native CSS :checked pseudo-class, which only works on actual form inputs (checkbox, radio) — a div never has a :checked state. Use a visually-hidden checkbox with peer, or aria-checked: variant instead
checked: requires JavaScript to be enabled on the element
The variant should be data-checked: for custom elements
checked: only works when combined with the peer modifier
questions.answer: checked: targets the native CSS :checked pseudo-class, which only works on actual form inputs (checkbox, radio) — a div never has a :checked state. Use a visually-hidden checkbox with peer, or aria-checked: variant instead
questions.explanation: CSS pseudo-classes like :checked only fire on native HTML form elements. A custom div-based component has no native checked state. Solutions: (1) use a hidden input type='checkbox' with peer to drive sibling styling, (2) use aria-checked attribute with the aria-checked: variant, or (3) drive the appearance via a conditional class from React state.
